resources.string: How elastic arteries stretch and recoil
Qualitative model of a large elastic artery, illustrated with an aortic segment. Wall motion and blood flow are shown separately. Scale, timing, and the width of the pulse are not measurements.
The aorta carries blood away from the left ventricle. Its inner lining faces the blood, its middle layer contains elastic sheets, and its outer layer supports the wall.
As the left ventricle ejects blood, pressure rises. The elastic wall stretches and temporarily stores part of the energy from ejection.
The pulse wave moves along the artery
The gold mark follows the wave of pressure and wall expansion; the red arrows show blood flow. The traveling wave is not a particular parcel of blood.
After the aortic valve closes and the ventricle relaxes, the expanded aorta recoils. That elastic recoil helps sustain downstream blood flow between ejections.
Stretch and recoil buffer the heart\'s intermittent output. This sketch shows the overall trend, not the exact flow pattern at every point in the arterial system.
